task: PR #1191's proposed_fix_sketch item 2: cache the resolved grammar path (module-level, keyed on the raw grammar_path string) instead of calling Path(...).resolve() inside every OpenUIIncrementalEngine.__init__ (10,967 calls / ~2.9s Path.resolve + ~2.2s os.path.realpath cumulative in that finding's one profiled decode record). Also empirically tested proposed_fix_sketch item 1 (share the _tail lru_cache across top-level candidates within one _openui_completion_domain call) before deciding whether to apply it.

item_1_tested_and_rejected.hypothesis: Sharing the per-candidate _tail lru_cache across all top-level candidates at one decode position lets a later candidate reuse an earlier one's proven (current, room) witness state instead of re-exploring it, cutting _build_openui_completion_forest call count.
item_1_tested_and_rejected.method: Implemented the hoist exactly as sketched (nodes_left reset per-candidate for fairness, _tail's lru_cache defined once per _openui_completion_domain call), then A/B measured _build_openui_completion_forest call count before vs after via git stash, same process, monkeypatched counter, on 6 real multi-candidate prefixes including the exact PREFIX9 (root = Card([b1,) from PR #1173's own regression test.
item_1_tested_and_rejected.result: zero call-count reduction on every prefix tested, witness content byte-identical before/after in all cases
item_1_tested_and_rejected.why: Different top-level candidates' token_ids diverge at the very first token by construction (initial.paths enumerates distinct actions at the same position), so their (current, room) recursive-search states never coincide within one _openui_completion_domain call -- there is nothing for a shared cache to hit. The safety property from the sketch ('sharing can only ever give a free win, never fewer real chances') held, but the win itself was empirically absent for the OpenUI grammar's actual candidate structure.
item_1_tested_and_rejected.decision: Reverted this half of the sketch (git checkout -- pack.py) rather than ship a no-benefit complexity addition; documented as a negative result so a future iteration does not re-attempt the identical hypothesis without new evidence.

summary: New _resolve_grammar_path(raw_path: str) -> str, @lru_cache(maxsize=8): returns str(Path(raw_path).resolve()), computed once per distinct raw path string.

OpenUIIncrementalEngine.__init__ now calls _resolve_grammar_path(str(path)) once and reuses the result for both _load_parser(resolved) and _load_lexer(resolved), instead of calling path.resolve() twice per init (once per callee).
change.why_safe: Path.resolve() is a pure, deterministic function of the raw path string within one process (no cwd/symlink change expected mid-run); _load_parser/_load_lexer's own @lru_cache is keyed on the resolved string exactly as before, so caching the resolve step cannot change which Lark/BasicLexer object either callee returns -- verified directly (test_equivalent_raw_paths_share_the_same_cached_parser_and_lexer).

reproduction.method: targeted micro-benchmark reproducing the finding's own profiled __init__ call count (10,967), same precedent as PR #1173's build_completion_forest before/after (not a full train/eval/checkpoint run)
reproduction.script_not_committed: bench_resolve.py (session scratchpad): times N=10967 OpenUIIncrementalEngine() constructions against the cached _resolve_grammar_path path, vs. an inlined reproduction of the exact pre-fix __init__ body (path.resolve() called directly, no cache) in the same process

item_2_applied.interpretation: Consistent 5.3x-5.6x speedup on OpenUIIncrementalEngine.__init__ itself (~0.63s-0.73s saved per 10,967 inits). Smaller in absolute terms than the finding's ~3.26s cumulative cProfile figure (which also includes the LALR-parser-frontend and other __init__-adjacent costs beyond the two explicit path.resolve() calls this fix targets), but a real, repeatable, isolated measurement of the specific syscall this fix eliminates -- roughly 2% of the ~29-34s total wall-clock budget of the finding's profiled records. Modest, not transformative: the dominant costs identified by the finding (Lark InteractiveParser.accepts(), 12.6s/23,530 calls) remain untouched by this change.
